title: Two goals in 15 games - what's going on with Gyokeres?
description: Arsenal have made an impressive start to the campaign but it has been a frustrating one for striker Viktor Gyokeres.
article_context:
Viktor Gyokeres has scored twice in all competitions this season
A Premier League trophy and 21 goals in his debut season - on paper things have worked out perfectly for Viktor Gyokeres since his £64m transfer to Arsenal.
But, even with those achievements, it has been a tough start to the current campaign for the 28-year-old striker.
The Swede has started just one Premier League game this season and is yet to score in his eight league appearances.
He has started three games in the Champions League, two in the Carabao Cup, and has scored just twice in 15 games in all competitions. Not the numbers he would have hoped for after last season's glory.
It is not just this season that has seen Gyokeres suitability questioned for Arsenal though.
Even though he scored more than 20 goals in his first season in all competitions as Arsenal ended their 22-year wait for a title, his all-round game had its critics.
It has been near enough a straight battle for the number nine role between Kai Havertz and Gyokeres since the Swedish international signed.
And Gyokeres was thrust into leading the line for Arsenal quicker and more frequently than planned after injury kept Havertz out for long periods last season.
Although the Swede may be the more natural finisher, Havertz's all-round play is considered superior with the German also one of Arteta's most trusted players for big games.
Gyokeres, a "win-now signing", was bought for his ability to find the net but also for how he could open up spaces for his team-mates, something they have praised him for.
But playing with his back to goal and linking up play is not natural to Gyokeres and his failure to hold up the ball or win duels with centre-backs has led to fan frustration.
Arteta has spoken about how the striker has been working on improving his hold-up play and connections, and there were hints of it in the Champions League win over Slavia Prague where Gyokeres assisted the opener and scored the winner in arguably his best game of the season.
Raya to miss Dortmund game but injury 'not serious'
A big reason that Gyokeres is not starting games is that Havertz is fit.
Last season, Havertz suffered with knee and hamstring issues which meant Gyokeres was the only option Arteta had.
Had Havertz been fit, he would have played a lot more and the fact that he started the Champions League final and the key match away at Manchester City in last season's title race back this up.
This season Gyokeres has just six starts and Arteta says that his gametime and situation is similar to other members in the squad.
"We have rotated the team a lot and used the competitions as well to give minutes to players and exposure because they are all starters in my opinion," Arteta said.
"Viktor's case is one of many that they have been in the same situation where they play more in the Premier League or more in the Champions League which is not bad, eh?"
Arteta is open with his players about their standing in the squad and said that Gyokeres has not approached him directly about a lack of minutes.
"We have conversations with every player to make sure that they understand what we are doing and to gather information about the way we are feeling and so far it has been very positive with Viktor and the rest of the team," he said.
The signing of Gyokeres is an interesting one in its own right.
The Arsenal recruitment team had done a lot of due diligence on signing, now Manchester United forward, Benjamin Sesko.
It is understood work on that deal had been done but a change of direction to sign Gyokeres happened after Andrea Berta became Arsenal sporting director.
Some around Arsenal have always thought that Gyokeres is not the usual forward that the Gunners would go for and his predicament of a lack of game time was always likely to happen, even if he did play a big part in them ending their trophy drought.
Gyokeres ended last season with 14 league goals but those strikes actually only won Arsenal two points on their way to winning the league.
That is because, although his penalty in the 1-0 win at Everton was the only goal of the game, Arsenal would have come away with a draw, so that strike factually only accounted for two points and not three.
But Gyokeres did put the Gunners ahead five times last season in the league which shows that, among the frustrating performances, he had plenty of impact.
Max Dowman stole the show with his goal in the 2-0 home win over Everton , when he became the youngest scorer in Premier League history, but it was Gyokeres' goal in the 89th-minute which put Arsenal ahead and although it did not lead to a point score on its own, it set them on the way.
Gyokeres also scored in the 4-1 north London derby win, putting Arsenal ahead when Kolo Muani had equalised after Eberechi Eze's opener.
It is unlikely that Gyokeres will be sold in January as he continues to get games in the Champions League and is a senior player who can score goals in big moments.
But if his lack of minutes in the league continue, Gyokeres, who is a driven and ambitious individual, will not want to be the player who is left out of the starting XI in the long term.

title: Defender Heaven open to leaving Man Utd
description: Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven is open to a loan move in January amid concerns over his game time as his side battles in the Premier League relegation zone.
article_context:
Heaven has made 32 appearances for Manchester United
Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven is open to a loan move in January amid concerns over his game time as his side battles in the Premier League relegation zone.
The 20-year-old centre-back is concerned about what United's current situation means for his development, after new manager Mauricio Pochettino left him as an unused substitute in Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool .
Now on his third manager in 21 months since joining from Arsenal in February 2025, Heaven accepts Pochettino may prefer more experienced options as United attempt to avoid a shock relegation.
The club have also been heavily linked with signing a centre-back in the coming January window, with targets said to include Fulham 's Calvin Bassey.
However, the Cottagers regard Bassey as an important player and would not encourage any interest.
Fulham and Barcelona are among the clubs to have expressed an interest in Heaven, with both having tried to sign him when he decided to leave Arsenal .
The England U20s defender's preference is believed to be a loan move, though he would also entertain permanent offers.
At United he has largely been used as a back-up option and, after enjoying a run in the team under former manager Ruben Amorim, he lost his place under Michael Carrick. He returned to the side only after an injury crisis hit the club last season.
Heaven is also capable of playing at left-back and in midfield, but does not expect to be trusted as a regular starter amid the instability at Old Trafford, with the club 19th in the league.
He is under contract until 2029 in a deal that includes an option for an extra year.

title: Man United win appeal over Yoro red card against Liverpool
description: Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.
article_context:
Manchester United have won their appeal over Leny Yoro 's red card against Liverpool .
The Frenchman was dismissed after eight minutes at Anfield after a challenge on Alexander Isak . On-field referee Sam Barrott decided Yoro had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity, a view backed up by VAR John Brooks.
United, who lost 4-0 in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as head coach, launched an appeal on Monday, insisting that Isak's heavy touch meant he would not have had the chance to score.
The Football Association announced on Tuesday that the claim of wrongful dismissal has been upheld and Yoro's one-match ban has been lifted.
A statement issued by the FA read: "Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.
"The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday Nov. 22."
Bruno Fernandes told the BBC that it was "never a red card," adding: "I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever.
"To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it's not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game."
Pochettino said: "I wasn't agreeing with the red card because I think the situation was when Isak control the ball, the ball wasn't in his control."
Kobbie Mainoo added: "The ball is already with the keeper when he's gone down, two players running at full speed. I mean, it's impossible to be a red, but it is what it is."
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola defended the referee's decision, saying: "[Yoro] is clearly the last man, it is clearly a foul. Would Alex or the 'keeper arrive first to the ball? We will never know. It's a clear foul, he's a last player, Alex goes against the 'keeper."
It's the second major refereeing error in a game involving United this season. In September, referee's body Pro Ref apologised after Erling Haaland 's goal at Old Trafford was mistakenly allowed to stand.
City, who were reduced to 10 men in the first half after Phil Foden 's red card, won the game 1-0.

title: Women's World Cup returning to U.S. shows how the game has grown since 1999
description: Women's soccer was forever changed when the U.S. hosted the 1999 World Cup. With it returning in 2031, ESPN charts the game's explosive growth.
article_context:
The Women's World Cup is coming back to the United States, with FIFA making the announcement Monday that the U.S., along with Costa Rica, Jamaica and Mexico will be co-hosting the 2031 edition of the tournament .
The 2031 World Cup will mark the first time that 48 teams will compete for the trophy, signifying the immense growth that women's soccer has enjoyed in recent years.
"This is a historic moment for our four countries, but the opportunity is much bigger than any one of us. Together with FIFA, we want to deliver the biggest and most impactful Women's World Cup in history and use its success to accelerate the growth of women's soccer around the world," said U.S. Soccer president Cindy Parlow Cone. "Our ambition is to create a tournament that not only inspires millions of players, but helps give them the opportunities to play, grow and pursue their dreams."
As such, it will have been 32 years since the U.S. first hosted the competition, when Brandi Chastain's iconic celebration capped off an epic run to the title by the U.S. women's national team . (The U.S. hosted the 2003 edition as well due to the SARS pandemic). Suffice it to say, the paths the women's game has trodden since make "The Odyssey" look like a Sunday cruise.
The U.S. witnessed two domestic leagues go under. Each failure seemed like a death knell for the sport, leaving fans to wonder whether there would ever be a viable club competition for the country's best players. Even as the third attempt, the NWSL , struggled to survive, it was deeply wounded by a sex abuse scandal . That outrage left scars that for some won't ever fully heal.
Yet the women's game has been nothing if not resilient. At club level, new investment poured into the NWSL, and with it, a level of stability and media attention that seemed unfathomable a decade ago. The league reported that total regular-season attendance rose to 2.5 million. According to Forbes, team valuations now average $200 million .
The developments abroad have been even more encouraging. For the first two decades after that fateful 1999 World Cup, the U.S. was the dominant power. The Americans won four World Cups in total and claimed another four Olympic gold medals following their victory in the inaugural competition in 1996.
As euphoric as those wins were for U.S. fans, it didn't necessarily speak to a healthy competition on a worldwide basis. But eventually, investment in other countries began to increase. Clubs in Spain, England and Mexico dedicated more resources to the women's game, and as a consequence rose up to challenge the sport's traditional powers, including the likes of the U.S., Japan , France and others.
That increase in investment and competition has seen some tangible results. Earlier this year, Club América claimed the Concacaf W Champions Cup, beating Gotham FC and the Washington Spirit along the way. At international level, Spain has assumed the mantle of the best women's national team in the world, claiming its first World Cup in 2023.
The oft-discussed gap between the USWNT and the rest of the world has vanished. Yes, the U.S. claimed Olympic gold again in 2024, but just a year before exited the World Cup in the round of 16. Claiming the top spot on the podium can no longer be expected like it was in the past.
That has resulted in plenty of introspection in the United States. The college game in the U.S. was once viewed as the gold standard for developing players. Not so now with players elsewhere entering professional environments at younger and younger ages.
Ali Krieger, Cristina Alexander and Jeff Kassouf debate the biggest storylines and break down the best highlights from women's soccer in the Americas. Stream on ESPN+ (U.S. only)
This is a healthy development for women's soccer. Steel sharpens steel, as the saying goes, and forcing clubs, leagues and other stakeholders to innovate to stay competitive is vital to the sport's overall growth.
That prospect is what makes the next five years so exciting. There are challenges to be sure. The fight for a bigger slice of resources -- from wages to sponsorship to infrastructure -- is never ending, but the trend in terms of gaining a bigger piece of those investments is decidedly upward.
Those benefits look set to extend to the U.S.'s co-hosts. Much like the men's World Cup in 2026, the U.S. figures to host the vast majority of matches, but at the very least, there will more eyeballs and interest in the countries that are co-hosting.
The five-year window before the tournament kicks off provides a lengthy on-ramp in terms of securing sponsorship and generating interest. On the field, will countries like Colombia , Morocco and Portugal continue to develop and threaten to further upset the status quo?
Women's soccer has navigated a challenging path to get to its current, stable place in the world sporting landscape. Next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil should provide a dose of rocket fuel to help create even more momentum ahead of 2031. Charting the sport's continued growth is something observers of all stripes will look upon with interest.

title: Del karma a los últimos festejos: cómo le fue a River en Alta Córdoba
description: El equipo de Ponzio visitará un escenario complejo, que incluye una extensa mala racha y dos recientes triunfos en la casa de Instituto.
article_context:
El festejo de Colidio en Alta Córdoba ante Instituto. Foto: Ariel Carreras.
Ante la confirmación de que Instituto no mudará su localía al Mario Alberto Kempes y recibirá a River en el estadio Monumental Presidente Perón, el equipo de Leonardo Ponzio ya sabe que tendrá que jugarse el pase a las semifinales del Clausura en un escenario con mucha historia. En la previa, la excursión al corazón de Alta Córdoba tendrá un fuerte contraste para el Millonario, con un historial general adverso que pesó durante décadas y un presente más alentador que incluye dos alegrías recientes en fila.
Si se toma la película completa de los 14 partidos oficiales que disputó el CARP en ese escenario -10 frente a la Gloria, dos contra Talleres y dos ante Racing de Córdoba-, la estadística global todavía marca números en rojo, con apenas dos victorias, ocho empates y cuatro derrotas. De hecho, durante medio siglo esa cancha fue un auténtico karma para Núñez: entre su primera visita el 24 de noviembre de 1974 (caída 2-1 frente a la T) y la de abril de 1990 , River encadenó 12 presentaciones sin poder ganar ni una sola vez en el tiempo reglamentario , con ocho empates y cuatro tropiezos.
En aquella época esquiva de los años 80, el Millonario sufrió golpes duros en el barrio cordobés: perdió 1-0 con Racing en diciembre de 1982 y padeció dos goleadas frente a Instituto, por 3-0 en noviembre de 1983 y por 4-1 el 8 de marzo de 1987. En el medio, coleccionó empates de todos los colores: 1-1 en 1982, dos 0-0 y un 2-2 a lo largo de 1984, otro 0-0 en febrero de 1988, dos pardas sin goles en 1989 -en la del 5 de marzo ante la Gloria se impuso por 5-4 en la definición por penales que otorgaba un punto extra en aquel certamen- y el 1-1 del 22 de abril de 1990.
Sin embargo, los antecedentes más cercanos cambiaron por completo la ecuación y le hacen un guiño al plantel actual. River acumula seis visitas consecutivas sin conocer la derrota en Alta Córdoba y quebró el maleficio por duplicado en sus últimas dos excursiones, ambas durante 2024 y remontando el resultado.
La primera de esas victorias fue el 15 de abril de 2024, por la última fecha de la Copa de la Liga. Aquella noche, el local arrancó arriba con un gol de penal de Damián Puebla , pero en el segundo tiempo apareció Facundo Colidio con un hat-trick inolvidable para sellar el 3-1 y el boleto a cuartos .
Casi 7 meses más tarde, el 6 de noviembre de 2024 por la Liga Profesional, la historia se repitió en otro partidazo. G regorio Rodríguez abrió la cuenta para la Gloria, Pablo Solari y Paulo Díaz lo dieron vuelta , Jonás Acevedo estampó el 2-2 parcial y, a ocho minutos del cierre, otra vez Colidio -verdugo con cuatro tantos en dos juegos en esa cancha- firmó el 3-2 definitivo tras un gran pase del Pity Martínez. Un antecedente fresco para creer.

title: FA chief signs NDA to view Fifa sell-off plot documents
description: Debbie Hewitt is among several football chiefs to view documents made available by Fifa, but cannot speak about them.
article_context:
Debbie Hewitt has been chair at the FA since 2022
Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) as a condition of viewing documents related to Fifa president Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup sell-off plot.
Hewitt was granted access to the information at the world governing body's headquarters in Zurich.
Earlier this month, Fifa said "key documents" on the abandoned plan to sell stakes in its tournaments to private investors would be made available to members of its council, but only in person and under "strict review protocols to preserve confidentiality".
Uefa had demanded Fifa release details about the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and answer questions relating to its decision-making.
Hewitt was among a group of council members who wrote to Fifa to say they were "concerned that any review would seemingly be limited to certain 'key documents'… which in turn would only be available for review under unknown 'strict review protocols'".
They also asked for clarity on what the protocols were, and "an explanation as to why Fifa considers such restrictions necessary since it is not clear why our rights are being limited in such a way".
The NDA means Hewitt cannot reveal what she has read, or comment about it publicly.
Fair Square, which campaigns for greater accountability in sport, told BBC Sport: "Debbie Hewitt and the FA didn't need to see the details of FFE to know that it was a gross abuse of presidential power.
"As a member association, the FA is entitled to hold the Fifa president accountable for his actions, and as a Fifa Council vice-president, Hewitt should have seen these plans as soon as they were hatched.
"They had the right to demand to see these documents, and should have exercised that right forcefully and publicly, rather than signing a gagging clause that puts Fifa and Infantino back in control."

Hewitt has previously criticised Infantino for a lack of transparency.
However, she embraced the Fifa president at a ceremony in Zurich on Monday when the UK bid to host the 2035 Women's World Cup was ratified at a special ceremony.
It is unclear whether she viewed the files on the same day, and which documents have been made available.
Last week, BBC Sport revealed the FA had considered challenging Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, and that it is backing French candidate Philippe Diallo in next year's presidential election.
Fifa has been approached for comment. Sources have previously indicated Fifa's ability to answer some questions is limited by legal action that Uefa launched in October in the US, requesting disclosure of evidence and documents, warning it could lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland.

title: Es oficial: la Copa América 2028 se jugará en los Estados Unidos
description: La Conmebol confirmó que USA volverá a ser sede del torneo continental por tercera vez en su historia. Participarán 16 selecciones, incluyendo seis de la Concacaf.
article_context:
Como había anticipado Olé , este martes se confirmó que la Copa América 2028 se jugará nuevamente en los Estados Unidos. La 49° edición del certamen continental se disputará entre el 9 de junio y el 9 de julio, y participarán 16 selecciones: además de las 10 de Conmebol , dirán presente seis representantes de Concacaf.
De esta manera se confirma que USA será anfitriona del certamen por tercera vez en la historia, después de hacerlo en 2016 (campeón Chile) y 2024 (Argentina). Tras disputar ambas finales, la Argentina buscará el tricampeonato de América.
¡Destino confirmado para la CONMEBOL Copa América 2028! Estados Unidos será el escenario de un nuevo capítulo en la historia del torneo de selecciones más antiguo del planeta. 🏆 pic.twitter.com/MGJLVyIjew
Los detalles relativos a las ciudades anfitrionas, las sedes y el calendario de partidos , así como información adicional sobre los mecanismos de clasificación para las selecciones nacionales de la Concacaf (será según las posiciones en la Copa de Oro 2027), se darán a conocer próximamente.
Alejandro Domínguez, presidente de la Conmebol, confirmó la noticia con un video en sus redes sociales y expresó: "La Copa América es mucho más que un torneo: es parte de nuestra identidad, de nuestra historia y de la grandeza del fútbol sudamericano. En 2028, llevaremos nuevamente esa pasión a los Estados Unidos, reafirmando nuestra histórica alianza con la Concacaf y nuestro compromiso compartido de seguir impulsando el crecimiento del fútbol en todo el continente. Esta nueva edición será una oportunidad más para demostrar que el fútbol no conoce fronteras y que, cuando 'creemos en grande', podemos llegar aún más lejos".
¡La CONMEBOL @CopaAmerica 2028 será en Estados Unidos! ¡El continente vibrará de nuevo con el torneo de selecciones más antiguo del mundo! pic.twitter.com/gvG2UR6qDQ
Por su parte, el presidente de la Concacaf y vicepresidente de la FIFA, Victor Montagliani, señaló: "Nuestra alianza estratégica con la Conmebol refleja el compromiso de nuestra Confederación con el crecimiento del fútbol y con la creación de más oportunidades para nuestras asociaciones miembro y sus selecciones nacionales. Tras nuestra colaboración en 2024, nos complace unir fuerzas nuevamente para traer la Copa América a nuestra región en 2028".
Además agregó: "Este acuerdo brindará a seis selecciones nacionales de la Concacaf una nueva oportunidad de competir contra algunas de las mejores del mundo, al tiempo que refuerza aún más la relevancia competitiva de nuestra Copa Oro de la Concacaf. Esperamos trabajar junto a la Conmebol, las sedes anfitrionas y otras partes clave para organizar un torneo de primer nivel que refleje la pasión, la calidad y el potencial del fútbol en todo el continente".
El comunicado también apunta que "la ampliación de esta alianza estratégica, aprobada por los Consejos de ambas Confederaciones, se fundamenta en la colaboración establecida en 2023, reafirmando el compromiso de crear nuevas oportunidades competitivas para sus selecciones nacionales y de fortalecer el fútbol en todo el continente".
